title: Error Handling Philosophy
concept: XIOM's error handling philosophy: fail fast and loudly. Catch bugs at the earliest possible point rather than letting corrupted state propagate.
why: The farther a bug propagates from its origin, the harder it is to debug. Failing fast at the contract boundary pinpoints the exact cause.
tips: Use contracts for bugs (things that should never happen) and Result for expected failures
Fail at the EARLIEST possible point — don't let bad data travel
A loud crash is better than silent corruption — you can't debug what you don't know about
Document which errors are recoverable (returned) vs unrecoverable (trapped)
common_mistakes: Returning error codes for programmer errors — these should be contracts
Using panic for recoverable errors — the caller can't handle a panic
Swallowing errors silently with empty catch blocks — always log or propagate
